title: Software Development Plan
description: Define your software lifecycle, responsibilities, verification approach, and release evidence.

sections.title: Document control & approvals
sections.prompt: Record product, document ID, version, owner, reviewers, approval dates, and change history.

sections.title: Scope & intended use
sections.prompt: Describe intended users, patient population, clinical setting, software boundaries, interfaces, and exclusions.

sections.title: Lifecycle & applicable requirements
sections.prompt: Identify applicable standards and jurisdictions, proposed software safety class and its risk-based justification, lifecycle activities, and tailoring rationale. Confirm these with qualified reviewers.

sections.title: Roles, resources & milestones
sections.prompt: Assign accountable owners, required competencies, tools, supplier oversight, deliverables, and review gates.

sections.title: Development & configuration management
sections.prompt: Define requirements, architecture, design, implementation, version control, baselines, third-party software/SOUP evaluation, and change-control practices.

sections.title: Risk management & traceability
sections.prompt: Connect hazards, risk controls, requirements, design, verification, and residual-risk decisions. Define how changes trigger reassessment.

sections.title: Verification, validation & release
sections.prompt: Specify test levels, acceptance criteria, independence where needed, anomaly disposition, release records, and approval responsibilities.

sections.title: Maintenance & problem resolution
sections.prompt: Define issue intake, security updates, impact assessment, maintenance testing, release communication, and end-of-support arrangements.

title: Requirements Traceability Matrix
description: Link requirements to hazards, design elements, verification evidence, and unresolved gaps.

sections.title: Requirement identity
sections.prompt: Assign stable identifiers and describe each testable requirement and its source.

sections.title: Risk & design links
sections.prompt: Reference related hazards, risk controls, and design elements; document rationale where a link is not applicable.

sections.title: Verification evidence
sections.prompt: Record test identifiers, measurable acceptance criteria, results, evidence references, and open gaps. Add rows for one-to-many relationships.

title: Software Risk Register
description: Capture hazardous situations, potential harms, controls, and the evidence behind risk decisions.

sections.title: Hazard analysis
sections.prompt: Describe the hazard, foreseeable event sequence, hazardous situation, and possible harm; include normal use, failure, and foreseeable misuse.

sections.title: Risk estimation & controls
sections.prompt: Use your approved risk-management method and acceptance criteria. Assign owners and identify controls and linked requirements.

sections.title: Residual risk review
sections.prompt: Reference control verification, residual-risk rationale, acceptability decisions, and unresolved actions. This worksheet is not a complete ISO 14971 risk-management file.

title: AI Model Evaluation Plan
description: Plan independent evaluation, subgroup analysis, clinical evidence, and acceptance criteria.

sections.title: Intended use & model baseline
sections.prompt: Document intended use, users, target population, clinical workflow, model version, inputs, outputs, and limitations.

sections.title: Evaluation data & leakage controls
sections.prompt: Record data provenance, permissions, inclusion/exclusion criteria, reference standards, label quality, and patient/site/time separation from training and tuning sets.

sections.title: Endpoints & acceptance criteria
sections.prompt: Prespecify clinically meaningful endpoints, performance metrics, confidence intervals, sample-size rationale, and acceptance thresholds. Avoid selecting criteria after reviewing test results.

sections.title: Subgroups & generalizability
sections.prompt: Define relevant patient groups and clinical sites, subgroup sample sizes, uncertainty reporting, and actions for material performance differences.

sections.title: Safety, usability & failure analysis
sections.prompt: Evaluate unsafe outputs, uncertainty handling, human oversight, automation bias, fallback behavior, and relevant workflow/usability risks.

sections.title: Execution & evidence review
sections.prompt: Assign owners and reviewers, lock model and dataset versions, document deviations, preserve results, and record independent review and go/no-go rationale.

sections.title: Lifecycle handoff
sections.prompt: Define deployment monitoring, drift thresholds, incident response, update evaluation, rollback, and change-control responsibilities.

title: Cloud Architecture Review
description: Review sensitive-data flows, shared responsibilities, security controls, and recovery readiness.

sections.title: System scope & data flows
sections.prompt: Identify services, environments, sensitive data including ePHI where applicable, storage locations, integrations, and trust boundaries. Attach a data-flow diagram.

sections.title: Vendor & shared responsibilities
sections.prompt: List providers, covered services, applicable agreements including BAAs where required, downstream services, and customer/provider control ownership.

sections.title: Identity & network boundaries
sections.prompt: Review unique identities, least privilege, privileged access, strong authentication, network segmentation, public exposure, and secrets management.

sections.title: Data protection & auditability
sections.prompt: Review encryption and key management, access/activity logging, integrity controls, retention, backups, and secure disposal; record applicable obligations and evidence.

sections.title: Resilience & incident response
sections.prompt: Document recovery objectives, restore-test evidence, failover assumptions, alert ownership, response contacts, and notification responsibilities.

sections.title: Findings & decisions
sections.prompt: For each finding record risk, evidence, recommendation, owner, due date, disposition, and follow-up verification. Document accepted risks and approval rationale.

title: Technical Discovery Brief
description: Align your team on the problem, scope, constraints, success measures, and delivery decisions.

sections.title: Problem & intended outcomes
sections.prompt: Describe the user problem, affected stakeholders, current workflow, and measurable outcomes. Separate confirmed facts from assumptions.

sections.title: Scope & boundaries
sections.prompt: List in-scope capabilities, exclusions, user groups, integrations, data sources, and dependencies.

sections.title: Constraints & obligations
sections.prompt: Capture security, privacy, regulatory, accessibility, performance, reliability, timeline, and budget constraints. Mark items requiring specialist review.

sections.title: Current system & delivery options
sections.prompt: Summarize current architecture and team capacity, reusable assets, technical debt, build/buy options, and major trade-offs.

sections.title: Risks & unknowns
sections.prompt: Identify critical assumptions, evidence needed, discovery experiments, owners, and decisions that block delivery.

sections.title: Milestones & acceptance
sections.prompt: Define proposed milestones, deliverables, acceptance measures, review owners, and the next decision gate.
